# ReproducibleNDI

[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

The goal of `ReproducibleNDI` is to provide a simple, tidy interface for calculating the **Neighborhood Deprivation Index (NDI)**, a composite measure of neighborhood-level socioeconomic status (SES), using data from the US Census Bureau's American Community Survey (ACS).

## What is the Neighborhood Deprivation Index?

The Neighborhood Deprivation Index is a composite score summarizing socioeconomic deprivation at the neighborhood level from a set of ACS variables. This package automatically fetches the required ACS data and computes the index for counties and census tracts.

Several NDI methodologies exist; the `type` parameter selects which one to compute. Currently implemented:

* **`type = "messer"`** — Messer et al. (2006), following the implementation of the [`ndi`](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ndi) package. A single principal component is extracted from 8 ACS-derived component variables (occupation, crowding, poverty, female-headed households, public assistance, income under $30k, education, unemployment). Available for **county and tract only** (see below); returns a quartile grouping (`NDIQuartile`).
* **`type = "powell_wiley"`** — Andrews et al. (2020), following the implementation of the `ndi` package. A promax-rotated PCA (Kaiser criterion for the number of factors) is fit to 13 ACS-derived component variables. Available for **county and tract only** (see below), and this package returns the **score only** (the population-weighted quintile grouping is not computed).

### Why the NDI is not available at block group

Neither method can be computed at block group from the same ACS tables it uses at tract and county. The Census Bureau does not publish every ACS table for block groups, and both methods need at least one table that stops at the census tract in every ACS 5-year release. This is a Census Bureau tabulation rule, not a limitation of this package or of `tidycensus`. Swapping in a different table would change the index, so the package does not do it: `computeNDI()` stops with an error for `geo = "block group"` (or `"cbg"`) with either method. For a block-group measure, use `computeICE()`.

The tables below list every component and whether its table is published for block groups (ACS 5-year, 2013–2024).

**Messer** (8 components, detailed tables only). Two tables are never published for block groups, and a third only from 2018:

| Component | Table | At block group |
|---|---|---|
| Males in management, business, science and arts occupations | `C24030` | Yes |
| Crowded housing (> 1 occupant per room) | `B25014` | Yes |
| Households below poverty | `B17017` | Yes |
| Female-headed households with dependent children | `B25115` | **No** (all years) |
| Households on public assistance or food stamps | `B19058` | **No** for 2013–2017; yes from 2018 |
| Households earning under $30,000 | `B19001` | Yes |
| Adults 25+ with less than high school | `B06009` | **No** (all years) |
| Unemployed (civilian labor force) | `B23025` | Yes |

**Powell-Wiley** (13 components). Seven come from the Data Profile (`DP`) and Subject (`S`) tables, which the Census Bureau does not publish below the tract; `tidycensus::get_acs()` fails with *"Block groups are not an available geography in the Data Profile and Subject Tables datasets."* One more detailed table is also not published for block groups:

| Component | Table | At block group |
|---|---|---|
| Median household income | `B19013` | Yes |
| Households with interest, dividends or net rental income | `B19054` | Yes |
| Households with public assistance income | `B19058` | **No** for 2013–2017; yes from 2018 |
| Median home value | `B25077` | Yes |
| Management, business, science and arts occupations | `C24060` | **No** (all years) |
| Female-headed households with own children | `B11005` | Yes |
| Owner-occupied housing units | `DP04` | **No** (Data Profile) |
| No telephone service | `DP04` | **No** (Data Profile) |
| Lacking complete plumbing | `DP04` | **No** (Data Profile) |
| High school or more (25+) | `S1501` | **No** (Subject table) |
| Bachelor's degree or more (25+) | `S1501` | **No** (Subject table) |
| Families below poverty | `S1702` | **No** (Subject table) |
| Unemployment rate | `S2301` | **No** (Subject table) |

"No" for a detailed table means `get_acs(geography = "block group", ...)` returns the table's variables as all `NA`. This was checked for every release from 2013 to 2024 (block-group ACS 5-year data starts in 2013) on all block groups of Bristol County, RI.

### Missing data: complete cases vs. pairwise correlation

Both NDI methods here fit their PCA on **complete cases only**. Any geography missing one or more of the method's component variables is dropped *before* the component correlation matrix is computed (listwise deletion); unless `impute = TRUE`, that geography then receives an `NA` index score and is flagged in the `annotation` column.

This is a deliberate deviation from the original [`ndi`](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ndi) package, which passes the component data straight to `psych::principal()` and therefore builds the correlation matrix from **pairwise-complete observations** (psych's default `use = "pairwise"`). Under that approach a partially-missing geography still contributes to every pairwise correlation for which it observes *both* variables.

Why this matters:

* The set of geographies that determine the component loadings can differ between the two approaches, so the fitted weights — and therefore the resulting scores — may differ slightly from `ndi`, most noticeably in scopes with substantial missingness.
* Complete-case fitting is the stricter, more transparent choice: the fitting sample is exactly the set of fully-observed geographies, with no geography contributing to some correlations but not others. Setting `impute = TRUE` (queen-contiguity spatial mean) fills the missing components so those geographies rejoin the complete-case set before the PCA is fit.

## Usage

```r
library(ReproducibleNDI)

# Requires a Census API key:
# tidycensus::census_api_key("YOUR_KEY_HERE", install = TRUE)

# Messer NDI for California tracts (2022 ACS5), PCA fit within the state
ndi_ca <- computeNDI(
  type   = "messer",
  geo    = "tract",
  year   = 2022,
  states = "CA",
  scope  = "state",
  impute = TRUE
)

head(ndi_ca$df_ndi)       # NDIImputed, NDIImputedQuartile, annotation
head(ndi_ca$df_ndi_raw)   # baseline NDI (no imputation) for comparison
```

Key options (mirroring `ReproducibleYostIndex`):

* **`scope`**: `"national"` (one PCA over all geographies), `"state"`, or `"county"` (PCA fit separately within each group).
* **`impute`**: spatial mean imputation of missing components using queen contiguity, optionally weighted by total population (`weight_var`).
* **`return_format`**: `"detailed"` (list of data frames + PCA object) or `"minimal"` (one data frame).

## Index of Concentration at the Extremes (ICE)

`computeICE()` computes Krieger's Index of Concentration at the Extremes, a separate family of measures from the NDI functions above. Each ICE measure is a self-contained per-geography ratio, `(Advantaged − Deprived) / Total`, ranging from −1 to +1 — so, unlike the NDI measures, it involves no cross-geography ranking or PCA and therefore has **no `scope` argument**.

`computeICE()` returns all five measures from `ndi::krieger`: `ICE_inc` (income), `ICE_edu` (education), `ICE_rewb` (race: NH-white vs NH-Black), `ICE_wbinc` (high-income white vs low-income Black), and `ICE_wpcinc` (income concentration among white households). Every ICE variable comes from ACS detailed (`B`) tables, so ICE is available at **county, tract, and block group**.

### ICE at block group: three measures, not five

At block group, `computeICE()` returns only **`ICE_inc`, `ICE_edu` and `ICE_rewb`**. `ICE_wbinc` and `ICE_wpcinc` are left out because they need household income by race (`B19001H`, `B19001B`), which the Census Bureau does not publish for block groups. As with the NDI, the package does not substitute another table. At county and tract all five measures are returned.

| Measure | Tables | At block group |
|---|---|---|
| `ICE_inc` | `B19001` | Yes |
| `ICE_edu` | `B15002` | Yes |
| `ICE_rewb` | `B03002` | Yes |
| `ICE_wbinc` | `B19001`, `B19001H`, `B19001B` | **No**: `B19001H` and `B19001B` are not published (all years) |
| `ICE_wpcinc` | `B19001`, `B19001H` | **No**: `B19001H` is not published (all years) |

This was checked the same way as for the NDI: `B19001H` and `B19001B` come back all `NA` for every block group in every ACS 5-year release from 2013 to 2024 (Bristol County, RI). Block-group ICE also requires `year >= 2013`.

```r
# ICE for Rhode Island tracts, 2022 (all five measures)
ice_ri <- computeICE(geo = "tract", year = 2022, states = "RI")
head(ice_ri$df_ice)

# Block-group ICE (ICE_inc, ICE_edu, ICE_rewb only), minimal output
ice_bg <- computeICE(geo = "block group", year = 2022, states = "RI",
                     return_format = "minimal")
```

Setting `impute = TRUE` fills missing ICE measures with the unweighted mean of their queen-contiguity neighbors. Only geographies with population are imputed or used as neighbors; a geography with no population keeps its raw values and is annotated `"No population"`. The result then also carries `nvar_imputed`, `nvar_still_missing`, `vars_imputed` and `annotation`, and the detailed output includes the pre-imputation baseline as `df_ice_raw`.

## Status

This package is in early development.

## Installation

You can install the development version of `ReproducibleNDI` from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("HanLabCollaboration/ReproducibleNDI")
```
